newsitem.title: USA: Urologix moves toward Japan marketing nod.
newsitem.headline: Urologix moves toward Japan marketing nod.

text.p: Urologix Inc, a developer of minimally invasive medical products for treating urological disorders, said Wednesday its system for treating enlarged prostate may soon win marketing approval in Japan.
The company said its distribution partner in Japan, Nihon Khoden, believes Japanese marketing approval for the Transurethral Thermo-ablation (T3) System is close at hand.
Urologix began European marketing of the T3 System at the start of its current fiscal year.
Boston Scientific Corp is serving as a distribution partner for the T3 System.

Urologix president Jack Meyer described increasing T3 System sales as encouraging. "However, it is still too early to measure adoption sell-through and utilization rates," he said in a statement. "The progress we've made is promising. We're moving along according to plan."

Meyer said the company increased capacity and production of the T3 System. "Now that we are equipped to handle the projected orders from Boston Scientific, we expect to begin building inventory in the third quarter in anticipation of orders from Japan, once approval is secured," he added.
In the United States, Urologix expects to file its Pre-Market Approval (PMA) application this quarter, as previously announced.
Earlier Wednesday, Urologix reported narrowing its December 31 second-quarter loss to $0.17 a share from a year-ago loss of $0.29 a share.
